headline: On last trading day, Sensex recovered 300 points, but Nifty recorded its longest weekly losing streak since 2020.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 28 September.

why: Rising crude oil prices above $100 and West Asia conflict risks weighed heavily on sentiment during the week.
A severe sell-off on Thursday dragged the Sensex down over 1,200 points, marking its worst day in 10 weeks.
Indian equities staged a partial rebound on Friday, with the Sensex gaining over 300 points led by auto and consumer durables.
Despite Friday's partial recovery, Indian benchmark indices logged their longest weekly losing streak since 2020.
whatHappening: The Central Government reduced its FY27 borrowing target by ₹1.2 trillion, planning to raise ₹7.8 trillion via gilts in H2.
The RBI Bulletin noted economic resilience but cautioned against downside risks from crude oil spikes and geopolitical tensions.
SIDBI withdrew its proposed ₹6,000 crore 3-year bond issue as market yields hardened.
Virtual pharma API company HRV is preparing for an IPO with a DRHP expected in H1 2027.
summary:
On the last trading session, Indian equities rebounded partially from Thursday's heavy sell-off as the Sensex gained over 300 points.
However, elevated crude oil prices caused benchmark indices to register their longest weekly losing streak since the 2020 COVID-19 crash.
The market is closed today for the weekend and will reopen on Monday, 28 September.
